\section{The space of truth assignments}

Throughout $\N=\{0,1,2,\dots\}$ and $\B=\{0,1\}$, whose elements we also read
as \textsf{false} and \textsf{true}.

\begin{definition}[Enumeration]
Fix a formal language with a computable enumeration $\varphi_0,\varphi_1,\dots$
of its sentences, each appearing exactly once.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Truth stream]
A \emph{truth stream} is a function $x:\N\to\B$; we write $x_k$ for $x(k)$
and read $x_k=1$ as ``$\varphi_k$ is true''. The set of all truth streams is
the Cantor space $\Cantor=\B^{\N}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Theory]
A \emph{theory} is a subset $T\subseteq\Cantor$. It is \emph{prefix-presented}
by the family $L_n(T)=\{(x_0,\dots,x_{n-1}):x\in T\}\subseteq\B^n$ of its
admissible finite prefixes, and we write $N_T(n)=|L_n(T)|$. Each $L_n(T)$ is
prefix-closed.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Agreement to depth $n$]
For $x,y\in\Cantor$ and $n\in\N$ write
$x\equiv_n y$ iff $x_k=y_k$ for all $k<n$.
\end{definition}

Agreement to depth $n$ is an equivalence relation with exactly $2^n$ classes,
each the \emph{cylinder} $[w]=\{x:(x_0,\dots,x_{n-1})=w\}$ of a word
$w\in\B^n$. It is monotone in $n$, and $x\equiv_0 y$ always holds.

\section{The first-disagreement metric}

\begin{definition}[First-disagreement metric]\label{def:metric}
For $x,y\in\Cantor$ set
\[
d(x,y)=\begin{cases}0,& x=y,\\ 2^{-m}, & m=\min\{k\in\N: x_k\neq y_k\}\ \text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
\]
\end{definition}

The minimum exists whenever $x\neq y$, since the disagreement set is a
nonempty subset of $\N$. The range of $d$ is $\{0\}\cup\{2^{-m}:m\in\N\}$, a
discrete set accumulating only at $0$. Symmetry, positivity and identity of
indiscernibles are immediate; the triangle inequality follows from the
stronger Theorem~\ref{thm:ultra}.

\subsection{Balls are prefix classes}

\begin{theorem}[Metric balls are cylinders]\label{thm:balls}
For all $x,y\in\Cantor$ and all $n\in\N$,
\[
d(x,y)\le 2^{-n}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\equiv_n y.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
($\Leftarrow$) If $x=y$ then $d=0\le 2^{-n}$. Otherwise the least
disagreement index $m$ satisfies $m\ge n$, since $x_k=y_k$ for all $k<n$;
as $t\mapsto 2^{-t}$ decreases, $d(x,y)=2^{-m}\le 2^{-n}$.

($\Rightarrow$) Contrapositive. If $x\not\equiv_n y$ there is $k<n$ with
$x_k\neq y_k$; then $x\neq y$ and the least disagreement index satisfies
$m\le k\le n-1$, so $d(x,y)=2^{-m}\ge 2^{-(n-1)}>2^{-n}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Geometry equals combinatorics]\label{cor:geo}
The closed ball $\bar B(x,2^{-n})$ equals the cylinder
$[x_0\cdots x_{n-1}]$. Hence the closed balls of radius $2^{-n}$ partition
$\Cantor$ into $2^n$ pieces, and a theory $T$ meets exactly $N_T(n)$ of them.
\end{corollary}

\subsection{The strong triangle inequality}

\begin{theorem}[Ultrametric inequality]\label{thm:ultra}
For all $x,y,z\in\Cantor$,
\[
d(x,z)\ \le\ \max\bigl(d(x,y),\,d(y,z)\bigr).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
If $x=z$ the left side is $0$. Otherwise put $\mu=\max(d(x,y),d(y,z))$. If
$\mu=0$ then $x=y=z$, a contradiction; so, the range of $d$ being
$\{0\}\cup\{2^{-n}\}$, we have $\mu=2^{-n}$ for some $n$. By
Theorem~\ref{thm:balls}, $x\equiv_n y$ and $y\equiv_n z$; agreement to depth
$n$ is transitive, so $x\equiv_n z$, and Theorem~\ref{thm:balls} in the
reverse direction gives $d(x,z)\le 2^{-n}=\mu$.
\end{proof}

The ultrametric inequality is \emph{exactly} the transitivity of prefix
agreement, transported across Theorem~\ref{thm:balls}; nothing analytic is
involved.

\begin{corollary}[Ultrametric phenomenology]\label{cor:phen}
In $(\Cantor,d)$:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em]
\item \emph{(Isosceles principle)} If $d(x,y)\neq d(y,z)$ then
$d(x,z)=\max(d(x,y),d(y,z))$.
\item \emph{(No centres)} If $y\in\bar B(x,\varepsilon)$ then
$\bar B(y,\varepsilon)=\bar B(x,\varepsilon)$.
\item \emph{(Nested or disjoint)} Any two closed balls are disjoint or one
contains the other.
\item \emph{(Clopen balls)} Every closed ball is open; $\Cantor$ is compact,
perfect and totally disconnected.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(1) If $d(x,y)<d(y,z)$ then $d(x,z)\le d(y,z)$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:ultra},
while $d(y,z)\le\max(d(y,x),d(x,z))$ forces $d(y,z)\le d(x,z)$ since
$d(y,x)<d(y,z)$. (2)--(3) follow from Corollary~\ref{cor:geo}: balls of a
fixed radius partition the space, and cylinders of different depths are
nested or disjoint. (4) Compactness is Tychonoff's theorem for $\B^{\N}$;
cylinders are clopen; distinct points are separated by a cylinder.
\end{proof}

Item (3) formalizes the intuition that research programmes \emph{branch}: two
theories that diverged at $\varphi_m$ can never again come closer than
$2^{-m}$, and the family of theories organizes itself as an infinite binary
tree of nested clusters.

\section{Box-counting dimension and the dimension of truth}

\begin{definition}[Box-counting dimension]
For bounded nonempty $S\subseteq\Cantor$ let $N_S(\varepsilon)$ be the minimal
number of closed balls of radius $\varepsilon$ covering $S$, and set
\[
\overline{\dim}_B S=\limsup_{\varepsilon\to0^+}\frac{\log N_S(\varepsilon)}{\log(1/\varepsilon)},\qquad
\underline{\dim}_B S=\liminf_{\varepsilon\to0^+}\frac{\log N_S(\varepsilon)}{\log(1/\varepsilon)} .
\]
When they agree, the common value is $\dim_B S$.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Prefix formula]\label{prop:prefix}
For any theory $T\subseteq\Cantor$,
\[
\overline{\dim}_B T=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log_2 N_T(n)}{n},\qquad
\underline{\dim}_B T=\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log_2 N_T(n)}{n}.
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
By Corollary~\ref{cor:geo} the closed balls of radius $2^{-n}$ partition
$\Cantor$ into cylinders, so any cover of $T$ at that scale must contain
every cylinder $T$ meets, and those cylinders suffice:
$N_T(2^{-n})=N_T(n)$ exactly. Since $\log(1/2^{-n})=n\log2$ the quotients
are $\log_2N_T(n)/n$; for $2^{-(n+1)}<\varepsilon\le2^{-n}$ the covering
number is unchanged, so no further limit points arise.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Dimension is entropy rate]
Proposition~\ref{prop:prefix} identifies $\dim_B T$ with the base-two entropy
rate of the prefix language of $T$: the average number of independent binary
decisions per statement. Dimension $1$ means asymptotic logical independence;
dimension $0$ means subexponential prefix growth. Since $N_T(n)\le 2^n$,
always $0\le\dim_BT\le1$.
\end{remark}

\subsection{The paired-dependency truth model}

\begin{definition}[Paired-dependency theory]\label{def:paired}
Suppose the enumeration interleaves \emph{primitive} statements and their
\emph{restatements}: for every $k$ the sentence $\varphi_{2k+1}$ is logically
equivalent to $\varphi_{2k}$, while $\varphi_0,\varphi_2,\varphi_4,\dots$ are
mutually logically independent. The associated theory is
\[
T_{1/2}=\{x\in\Cantor: x_{2k+1}=x_{2k}\ \text{for all }k\}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Prefix count]\label{lem:count}
$N_{T_{1/2}}(n)=2^{\lceil n/2\rceil}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
A word $w\in\B^n$ is admissible iff $w_{2k+1}=w_{2k}$ whenever $2k+1<n$. The
free coordinates are exactly the even ones below $n$, of which there are
$\lceil n/2\rceil$, and every assignment of them extends uniquely.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Truth has a nontrivial fractal dimension]\label{thm:dim}
The paired-dependency truth set satisfies
\[
\dim_B T_{1/2}=\tfrac12,\qquad\text{and in particular}\qquad 0<\dim_BT_{1/2}<1 .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:count} and Proposition~\ref{prop:prefix},
\[
\frac{\log_2N_{T_{1/2}}(n)}{n}=\frac{\lceil n/2\rceil}{n}\in\Bigl[\tfrac12,\ \tfrac12+\tfrac{1}{2n}\Bigr],
\]
and squeezing gives the limit $\tfrac12$; the strict inequalities are
numerical.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Consequences: sparse but not negligible}

\begin{corollary}[Sparsity]\label{cor:sparse}
$T_{1/2}$ is null for the fair-coin measure $\mu$ on $\Cantor$: a truth
assignment generated by independent fair coin flips is inadmissible with
probability $1$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$\mu([w])=2^{-n}$ for $w\in\B^n$, so
$\mu(T_{1/2})\le N_{T_{1/2}}(n)2^{-n}=2^{\lceil n/2\rceil-n}\to0$. More
generally any theory with $\overline{\dim}_BT<1$ is $\mu$-null, since
$N_T(n)2^{-n}=2^{n(\log_2N_T(n)/n-1)}\to0$ exponentially.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Abundance]\label{cor:abund}
$T_{1/2}$ has cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$ and is homeomorphic to $\Cantor$; in
particular it is uncountable, compact and perfect.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The coordinate-doubling map
$\Phi(a_0,a_1,a_2,\dots)=(a_0,a_0,a_1,a_1,a_2,a_2,\dots)$ is a bijection of
$\Cantor$ onto $T_{1/2}$ with $d(\Phi a,\Phi b)\in\{2^{-2m},2^{-2m-1}\}$
whenever $d(a,b)=2^{-m}$, hence a homeomorphism onto its image. Positive box
dimension alone already forces uncountability, since countable compact sets
have box dimension~$0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Reading the two inequalities]
$\dim_B<1$ says truth is \emph{rare}: admissible streams occupy an
exponentially shrinking fraction of all streams. $\dim_B>0$ says truth is
\emph{not negligible}: there are continuum-many complete admissible
extensions, so no finite or countable list captures them. Positivity of
dimension is a geometric shadow of incompleteness: independent decisions keep
arriving, forever, at a positive asymptotic rate.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Robustness]\label{rem:robust}
Nothing depends on the pattern ``evens free, odds forced''. If
$R\subseteq\{0,\dots,m-1\}$ is a set of residues and $T_R$ is the theory in
which coordinates in residue classes $R$ modulo $m$ are free while the others
are determined by earlier coordinates, the same argument gives
$N_{T_R}(n)=2^{|R|n/m+O(1)}$ and $\dim_BT_R=|R|/m$, so every rational value
in $[0,1]$ is realised.
\end{remark}

\section{The signed Boolean cube and its spectral projections}

Prefixes of length $n$ are the vertices of the cube $Q_n=\B^n$; instead of
counting them asymptotically we now measure subsets of a fixed cube
spectrally.

\begin{definition}[Cube functions]
$Q_0$ is the singleton containing the empty word and
$Q_{n+1}=\{bx: b\in\B,\ x\in Q_n\}$. A \emph{cube function} is a map
$v:Q_n\to\R$. For $v:Q_{n+1}\to\R$ and $b\in\B$ write $v_b:Q_n\to\R$,
$v_b(x)=v(bx)$, for the restriction to a facet.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Signed adjacency operator]\label{def:signed}
Define $A_n$ on cube functions by $A_0v=0$ and
\[
(A_{n+1}v)(0x)=(A_nv_0)(x)+v_1(x),\qquad (A_{n+1}v)(1x)=v_0(x)-(A_nv_1)(x).
\]
In block form, with facets ordered $0\ast$ then $1\ast$,
\[
A_{n+1}=\begin{pmatrix} A_n & I_{2^n}\\ I_{2^n} & -A_n\end{pmatrix},\qquad
A_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
\end{definition}

Replacing $-A_n$ by $+A_n$ recovers the ordinary hypercube adjacency
operator, whose spectrum is $\{n-2i:0\le i\le n\}$. The single sign change
collapses the spectrum to two values.

\subsection{Linearity}

\begin{theorem}[Additivity and homogeneity]\label{thm:linear}
For all $n$, all cube functions $v,w:Q_n\to\R$ and all $c\in\R$,
\[
A_n(v+w)=A_nv+A_nw,\qquad A_n(c\,v)=c\,A_nv .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Induction on $n$; both sides vanish for $n=0$. For the step, evaluate at a
vertex $bx$ and split on $b$. For $b=0$, using $(v+w)_b=v_b+w_b$,
\[
(A_{n+1}(v+w))(0x)=\bigl(A_n(v_0+w_0)\bigr)(x)+v_1(x)+w_1(x),
\]
and the inductive hypothesis rewrites the first term as
$(A_nv_0)(x)+(A_nw_0)(x)$; regrouping yields
$(A_{n+1}v)(0x)+(A_{n+1}w)(0x)$. The case $b=1$ is identical up to the sign.
Homogeneity is the same induction with $(cv)_b=c\,v_b$ and distributivity.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:neg}
$A_n0=0$ and $A_n(-v)=-A_nv$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$A_n0=A_n(0\cdot0)=0$, and $A_nv+A_n(-v)=A_n0=0$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The square law}

\begin{theorem}[Square of the signed operator]\label{thm:square}
For every $n$, $A_n^2=n\,\mathrm{id}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Induction in block form: $A_0^2=0$, and assuming $A_n^2=nI$,
\[
A_{n+1}^2=\begin{pmatrix}A_n&I\\ I&-A_n\end{pmatrix}^2
=\begin{pmatrix}A_n^2+I& A_n-A_n\\ A_n-A_n& I+A_n^2\end{pmatrix}
=(n+1)I,
\]
the off-diagonal blocks cancelling identically.
\end{proof}

Consequently the only possible eigenvalues of $A_n$ are $\pm\sqrt n$, and
$A_n^{-1}=n^{-1}A_n$ for $n\ge1$. The decomposition itself is supplied
constructively by the next results.

\subsection{Explicit spectral projections}

\begin{definition}[Spectral parts]\label{def:proj}
Let $n\ge1$ and $r\in\R$ with $r\neq0$ and $r^2=n$. For $v:Q_n\to\R$ define
\[
P_+^{(r)}v=\tfrac12\bigl(v+r^{-1}A_nv\bigr),\qquad
P_-^{(r)}v=\tfrac12\bigl(v-r^{-1}A_nv\bigr),
\]
pointwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Reconstruction]\label{thm:recon}
For every cube function $v$, $\ P_+^{(r)}v+P_-^{(r)}v=v$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Pointwise, $\tfrac12(a+t)+\tfrac12(a-t)=a$ with $a=v(x)$ and
$t=r^{-1}(A_nv)(x)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Eigenfunction property]\label{thm:eigen}
Let $r\neq0$ with $r^2=n$. Then for every cube function $v$,
\[
A_n\bigl(P_+^{(r)}v\bigr)=r\,P_+^{(r)}v,\qquad
A_n\bigl(P_-^{(r)}v\bigr)=-r\,P_-^{(r)}v .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Apply $A_n$ and use Theorem~\ref{thm:linear} (and Corollary~\ref{cor:neg} in
the negative case):
\[
A_n\bigl(P_\pm^{(r)}v\bigr)=\tfrac12\bigl(A_nv\pm r^{-1}A_n(A_nv)\bigr)
=\tfrac12\bigl(A_nv\pm r^{-1}n\,v\bigr)
\]
by Theorem~\ref{thm:square}. Since $r^{-1}n=r^{-1}r^2=r$, this equals
$\tfrac12(A_nv\pm r\,v)=\pm r\,P_\pm^{(r)}v$, the last equality being checked
by expanding
$\pm r\cdot\tfrac12(v\pm r^{-1}A_nv)=\tfrac12(\pm r\,v+r\,r^{-1}A_nv)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Complementary idempotents]\label{cor:idem}
For $n\ge1$ and $r\neq0$ with $r^2=n$, the operators $P_\pm^{(r)}$ are linear
and satisfy
\[
\bigl(P_\pm^{(r)}\bigr)^2=P_\pm^{(r)},\qquad
P_+^{(r)}P_-^{(r)}=P_-^{(r)}P_+^{(r)}=0,\qquad
P_+^{(r)}+P_-^{(r)}=\mathrm{id},
\]
so the space of cube functions is the internal direct sum of
$E_{+r}=\im P_+^{(r)}$ and $E_{-r}=\im P_-^{(r)}$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Linearity is inherited from $A_n$. If $u=P_+^{(r)}v$ then $A_nu=ru$ by
Theorem~\ref{thm:eigen}, so $P_+^{(r)}u=\tfrac12(u+r^{-1}ru)=u$ and
$P_-^{(r)}u=\tfrac12(u-r^{-1}ru)=0$; symmetrically for the other order. If
$u\in E_{+r}\cap E_{-r}$ then $ru=A_nu=-ru$, so $u=0$ as $r\neq0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Equal multiplicities]\label{prop:mult}
For $n\ge1$, $\dim E_{+r}=\dim E_{-r}=2^{n-1}$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
All diagonal entries of $A_n$ vanish, so $\tr A_n=0$. By
Corollary~\ref{cor:idem} the two eigenspaces exhaust the $2^n$-dimensional
space, so $0=r\dim E_{+r}-r\dim E_{-r}$ with
$\dim E_{+r}+\dim E_{-r}=2^n$ and $r\neq0$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Why the halving matters}

\begin{theorem}[Degree bound for majorities; Huang]\label{thm:huang}
Let $S\subseteq Q_n$ with $|S|\ge 2^{n-1}+1$. Then the induced subgraph of the
hypercube on $S$ has maximum degree at least $\sqrt n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch (context)]
By Proposition~\ref{prop:mult}, $E_{+\sqrt n}$ has dimension $2^{n-1}$, while
the space of functions supported on $S$ has dimension $|S|\ge2^{n-1}+1$; two
subspaces of $\R^{Q_n}$ whose dimensions sum to more than $2^n$ intersect
nontrivially, so there is a nonzero $+\sqrt n$-eigenfunction supported on $S$.
Cauchy interlacing then gives that the principal submatrix $A_n[S]$ has
largest eigenvalue at least $\sqrt n$, and the largest eigenvalue of a
symmetric $\pm1$-signed adjacency matrix is at most the maximum degree of the
underlying graph.
\end{proof}

Combined with the Gotsman--Linial equivalence, Theorem~\ref{thm:huang}
resolves the sensitivity conjecture: sensitivity is at least the square root
of degree, hence polynomially related to block sensitivity, certificate
complexity and decision-tree depth. Definition~\ref{def:proj} makes the
witnessing eigenfunction computable: apply $P_+^{(\sqrt n)}$ to any function
it does not annihilate, at the cost of one application of $A_n$.

\section{The bridge: counting is spectral}

\begin{definition}[Finite-state theory]
A theory $T$ is \emph{finite-state} if its admissible prefixes are the label
sequences of walks from a distinguished start state in a finite directed
graph with bit-labelled edges. Write $M$ for its adjacency matrix and
$\rho(M)$ for the spectral radius.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Dimension is a spectral radius]\label{prop:bridge}
For a nonempty finite-state theory $T$ presented by a primitive matrix $M$,
\[
\dim_B T=\frac{\log\rho(M)}{\log 2}=\log_2\rho(M).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The number of walks of length $n$ from the start state is the corresponding
row sum of $M^n$; by Perron--Frobenius this grows like $c\rho(M)^n$ with
$c>0$ for primitive $M$. Hence $N_T(n)=\Theta(\rho(M)^n)$ and
Proposition~\ref{prop:prefix} applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{example}[The golden-mean theory]\label{ex:golden}
Let $T_\varphi$ be the theory in which no two consecutive statements are
simultaneously true --- the crudest consistency taboo. Its transfer matrix is
$M=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ with spectral
radius the golden ratio $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$; prefix counts obey the
Fibonacci recurrence $N(n)=N(n-1)+N(n-2)$ with $N(0)=1$, $N(1)=2$. Hence
\[
\dim_B T_\varphi=\log_2\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}\approx0.694242,
\]
again strictly between $0$ and $1$.
\end{example}

\begin{example}[Paired dependency, revisited]
$T_{1/2}$ is presented by an alternating pair of transfer steps: a
\emph{free} step, doubling the number of admissible words, followed by a
\emph{forced} step, preserving it. The product of the two step matrices has
spectral radius $2$, so the per-step growth rate is $\sqrt2$ and the
dimension is $\log_2\sqrt2=\tfrac12$, in agreement with
Theorem~\ref{thm:dim}. For a period-$m$ presentation the dimension is
$\log_2\rho(M_{m-1}\cdots M_0)/m$.
\end{example}

Thus the fractal dimension of a locally constrained truth set \emph{is} the
logarithm of an eigenvalue, and in particular is always the base-two
logarithm of an algebraic number.

\section{Algorithms}

\begin{algorithmbox}[Metric evaluation and ball membership]
Given two truth streams as oracles and a depth budget $D$, scan
$k=0,1,\dots,D$ until $x_k\neq y_k$; return $2^{-k}$ at the first
disagreement, and ``$\le 2^{-D}$'' otherwise. By Theorem~\ref{thm:balls} the
same scan decides ball membership. Cost: $O(\min(m,D))$ oracle calls, where
$m$ is the first disagreement index.
\end{algorithmbox}

\begin{algorithmbox}[Prefix counting and dimension estimation]
Given a decidable admissibility predicate on words, enumerate the
prefix-closed language level by level: from the list $L_n$ of admissible
words of length $n$, form $L_{n+1}$ by appending each bit and filtering. Then
$N(n)=|L_n|$ and the estimate is $\log_2N(n)/n$. Cost:
$O(\sum_{k\le n}N(k))$ predicate calls; for a finite-state theory this is
replaced by matrix powering,
$N(n)=\mathbf e_{\mathrm{start}}^{\top}M^n\mathbf 1$, in $O(s^3\log n)$
operations for $s$ states.
\end{algorithmbox}

\begin{algorithmbox}[Signed operator and spectral splitting]
Represent a cube function as an array of $2^n$ reals indexed by bitmask.
Compute $A_nv$ by the recursion of Definition~\ref{def:signed}, splitting the
array in halves, recursing, and combining as
$\mathrm{low}'+\mathrm{high}$ and $\mathrm{low}-\mathrm{high}'$. Cost
$T(2^n)=2T(2^{n-1})+O(2^n)=O(n2^n)$, a butterfly of the same shape as a fast
Walsh--Hadamard transform. Then $P_\pm v=(v\pm r^{-1}A_nv)/2$ with
$r=\sqrt n$, and all verifications cost $O(n2^n)$.
\end{algorithmbox}

\section{Discussion}

\subsection{What ``dimension of truth'' does and does not say}
The theorems here are about a \emph{model}: an enumeration together with a
specification of which prefix patterns are admissible. The number $\tfrac12$
is not an absolute constant of mathematics; it is the entropy rate of a
deliberately simple dependency structure --- one restatement per primitive
assertion. What is model-independent is the framework: every prefix-presented
theory has well-defined upper and lower dimensions in $[0,1]$; dimension $1$
characterises asymptotic logical independence; dimension $0$ characterises
subexponential prefix growth; everything strictly between is the fractal
regime, where truth is null yet uncountable. Sparsity formalizes ``most
conceivable worlds are inconsistent''; positivity formalizes ``no finite
description exhausts truth''. Where a given formal system sits between the
poles is an empirical question about its dependency structure, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:bridge} says that for finitely presentable structures
the answer is computable.

\subsection{Why ultrametricity is the right ambient geometry}
An objection to metrizing theory space is that any metric seems arbitrary.
But the first-disagreement metric is derived rather than chosen: it is the
unique, up to bi-Lipschitz equivalence and reparametrization of the radius
scale, metric whose balls are the prefix classes --- and the prefix classes
are precisely the sets distinguishable by a finite amount of inspection.
Ultrametricity is then a theorem, not an assumption, and its consequences
match the phenomenology of theory-branching.

\subsection{The two rulers compared}
Box dimension is an asymptotic, cardinality-based invariant: it sees only how
many vertices of $Q_n$ survive in the exponential limit. The signed operator
gives finite-$n$, structural information: it constrains not how many vertices
a set has but how they are arranged, forcing local density $\sqrt n$ on any
majority. A set of $2^{n-1}+1$ vertices has counting dimension $1$, so the
metric ruler is blind to Theorem~\ref{thm:huang}; conversely the spectral
ruler says nothing about a set of $2^{n/2}$ vertices. The two are
complementary, and Proposition~\ref{prop:bridge} is where they touch.

\subsection{Sharpness}
The value $\tfrac12$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:dim} is exact: the bounds pinch to
within $1/(2n)$ at every finite $n$, so convergence is $O(1/n)$. The exponent
$\sqrt n$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:huang} is sharp. And the eigenvalue structure of
$A_n$ is as rigid as possible: two eigenvalues, equal multiplicities,
explicit projections.

\section{Future directions}

\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em]
\item \textbf{Periodic-coordinate dimension formula.} For every $m>0$ and
every set of residues $R\subseteq\{0,\dots,m-1\}$, the subset of Cantor
streams whose coordinates outside $R$ are fixed has Hausdorff dimension
$|R|/m$ in the first-disagreement metric.
\item \textbf{Hausdorff/box agreement for periodic truth sets.} For every
periodic-coordinate theory, its Hausdorff dimension in the
first-disagreement metric equals the box dimension of its finite-prefix
family.
\item \textbf{Bi-Lipschitz invariance under bounded coordinate
permutations.} If a permutation $\sigma$ of $\N$ has bounded displacement,
i.e.\ $|\sigma(n)-n|\le C$ for all $n$, then precomposition by $\sigma$
preserves the box dimension of every prefix-closed theory.
\item \textbf{Finite-state truth dimensions are algebraic.} For every
nonempty binary subshift presented by a finite directed graph with adjacency
matrix $A$, the prefix box dimension is $\log(\rho(A))/\log2$, hence the
base-two logarithm of an algebraic number.
\item \textbf{Golden-mean truth set.} The set of Boolean streams with no two
consecutive true values has Hausdorff and box dimension
$\log_2\bigl((1+\sqrt5)/2\bigr)$, strictly between $0$ and $1$.
\end{enumerate}

On the spectral side, natural next steps are: an explicit basis of
$E_{+\sqrt n}$ obtained by applying $P_+$ to vertex indicators; quantitative
refinements of Theorem~\ref{thm:huang} for sets of size $(1-\delta)2^{n-1}$;
and signed operators over larger alphabets, where one asks for the analogue
of $A^2=nI$ and its consequences for sensitivity-type measures.

\section{Conclusion}

Fix an enumeration of statements, declare two theories close when they agree
deep into that enumeration, and a rigid geometry appears unbidden: closed
balls are prefix classes, the strong triangle inequality holds, and the space
is a compact ultrametric Cantor set in which theories cluster hierarchically
and never partially overlap. In that geometry the box dimension of a theory
is the entropy rate of its prefix language, and for a truth model with one
restatement per primitive assertion the dimension is exactly $\tfrac12$ ---
strictly between the zero-dimensional extreme of a categorical theory and the
full-dimensional extreme of total logical anarchy. Truth so modelled is a
fractal dust: measure zero under fair coin flips, yet of cardinality
continuum.

The vertices being counted are those of Boolean cubes, and those cubes admit
a sharper instrument. Signing half the edges by the recursion
$A_{n+1}=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}A_n&I\\ I&-A_n\end{smallmatrix}\right)$
produces an operator with $A_n^2=nI$ and explicit complementary projections
$P_\pm=\tfrac12(\mathrm{id}\pm r^{-1}A_n)$ onto its two eigenspaces, each of
dimension exactly $2^{n-1}$. That exact halving forbids any majority of cube
vertices from being locally sparse, and is the algebraic core of the
resolution of the sensitivity conjecture. Counting and spectra converge: for
locally constrained theories the dimension of truth is the logarithm of a
spectral radius.

import random
from fractions import Fraction
from typing import Callable, Iterable, List, Sequence, Tuple

Stream = Callable[[int], int]          # a truth stream, coordinate oracle
Word = Tuple[int, ...]                 # a finite prefix
CubeFn = List[float]                   # array of 2^n reals, indexed by bitmask

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART I.1 -- the first-disagreement metric
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def first_disagreement(x: Stream, y: Stream, depth: int = 64) -> int | None:
    """Least index k < depth with x(k) != y(k); None if no disagreement found."""
    for k in range(depth):
        if x(k) != y(k):
            return k
    return None


def cantor_dist(x: Stream, y: Stream, depth: int = 64) -> float:
    """d(x, y) = 2^-m where m is the first disagreement index (0 if none)."""
    m = first_disagreement(x, y, depth)
    return 0.0 if m is None else 2.0 ** (-m)


def agree_to(n: int, x: Stream, y: Stream) -> bool:
    """x =_n y : the streams agree on every coordinate k < n."""
    return all(x(k) == y(k) for k in range(n))


def ball_is_cylinder_check(x: Stream, y: Stream, n: int, depth: int = 64) -> bool:
    """Theorem: d(x,y) <= 2^-n  <=>  x and y agree on the first n coordinates."""
    return (cantor_dist(x, y, depth) <= 2.0 ** (-n) + 1e-15) == agree_to(n, x, y)


def ultrametric_check(x: Stream, y: Stream, z: Stream, depth: int = 64) -> bool:
    """Theorem: d(x,z) <= max(d(x,y), d(y,z))."""
    return cantor_dist(x, z, depth) <= max(
        cantor_dist(x, y, depth), cantor_dist(y, z, depth)
    ) + 1e-15


def random_stream(rng: random.Random) -> Stream:
    """A lazily-generated, memoised random truth stream."""
    memo: dict[int, int] = {}

    def s(k: int) -> int:
        if k not in memo:
            memo[k] = rng.randint(0, 1)
        return memo[k]

    return s


def perturbed_stream(base: Stream, split: int, rng: random.Random) -> Stream:
    """Agrees with `base` below `split`, then flips and goes its own way."""
    tail = random_stream(rng)

    def s(k: int) -> int:
        if k < split:
            return base(k)
        if k == split:
            return 1 - base(k)
        return tail(k)

    return s


def demo_metric(seed: int = 20260803) -> None:

    print(f"{'branch depth m':>16} {'d(x,y)':>14} {'2^-m':>14}   balls=cylinders?")
    for m in range(0, 9):
        y = perturbed_stream(base, m, rng)
        d = cantor_dist(base, y)
        ok = all(ball_is_cylinder_check(base, y, n) for n in range(0, 12))
        print(f"{m:>16} {d:>14.9f} {2.0 ** -m:>14.9f}        {ok}")

    print("\nStrong triangle inequality on 20000 random triples:")
    bad = 0
    isosceles = 0
    for _ in range(20000):
        depth = rng.randint(0, 10)
        x = random_stream(rng)

        z = perturbed_stream(y, depth, rng)

        big = max(dxy, dyz, dxz)

    print(f"  triangles with two equal longest sides      : {isosceles}/20000")
    print("  (in an ultrametric space EVERY triangle is isosceles)")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART I.2 -- prefix counting and box dimension
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def admissible_prefixes(
    predicate: Callable[[Word], bool], n: int
) -> List[Word]:
    """All admissible words of length n, grown level by level (prefix-closed)."""
    level: List[Word] = [()]
    for _ in range(n):
        nxt: List[Word] = []
        for w in level:
            for b in (0, 1):
                cand = w + (b,)
                if predicate(cand):
                    nxt.append(cand)
        level = nxt
    return level


def paired_dependency(w: Word) -> bool:
    """Every odd coordinate restates the even one before it: w[2k+1] = w[2k]."""
    return all(w[i] == w[i - 1] for i in range(1, len(w), 2))


def golden_mean(w: Word) -> bool:
    """No two consecutive statements are simultaneously true."""
    return all(not (w[i] == 1 and w[i + 1] == 1) for i in range(len(w) - 1))


def unconstrained(w: Word) -> bool:
    """Total logical anarchy: every pattern admissible."""
    return True


def box_dimension_estimates(
    predicate: Callable[[Word], bool], max_n: int
) -> List[Tuple[int, int, float]]:
    """Returns (n, N(n), log2 N(n) / n) for n = 1..max_n."""
    out: List[Tuple[int, int, float]] = []
    for n in range(1, max_n + 1):
        count = len(admissible_prefixes(predicate, n))
        out.append((n, count, math.log2(count) / n))
    return out


def transfer_matrix_count(matrix: Sequence[Sequence[int]],
                          start: Sequence[int], n: int) -> int:
    """Number of length-n walks: e_start^T M^n 1, by repeated vector-matrix mult."""
    vec = list(start)
    size = len(matrix)
    for _ in range(n):
        vec = [sum(vec[i] * matrix[i][j] for i in range(size)) for j in range(size)]
    return sum(vec)


def spectral_radius_2x2(m: Sequence[Sequence[int]]) -> float:
    """Largest eigenvalue modulus of a 2x2 matrix, via the quadratic formula."""
    tr = m[0][0] + m[1][1]
    det = m[0][0] * m[1][1] - m[0][1] * m[1][0]
    disc = tr * tr - 4 * det
    if disc >= 0:
        r = math.sqrt(disc)
        return max(abs((tr + r) / 2), abs((tr - r) / 2))
    return math.sqrt(abs(det))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART II -- the signed adjacency operator on the Boolean cube
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def signed_adj(n: int, v: CubeFn) -> CubeFn:
    """(A_n v), where A_0 = 0 and A_{n+1} = [[A_n, I], [I, -A_n]].

    Vertices of Q_n are bitmasks 0..2^n-1; the LEADING bit is the high bit,
    so the low half of the array is the facet 0*, the high half is 1*.
    Cost: O(n 2^n) -- a butterfly, like a fast Walsh-Hadamard transform.
    """
    if n == 0:
        return [0.0]
    half = 1 << (n - 1)
    low, high = v[:half], v[half:]
    a_low, a_high = signed_adj(n - 1, low), signed_adj(n - 1, high)
    return [a_low[i] + high[i] for i in range(half)] + [
        low[i] - a_high[i] for i in range(half)
    ]


def signed_adj_matrix(n: int) -> List[List[float]]:
    """Explicit 2^n x 2^n matrix of A_n (columns = images of basis vectors)."""
    size = 1 << n
    cols = []
    for j in range(size):
        e = [0.0] * size
        e[j] = 1.0
        cols.append(signed_adj(n, e))
    return [[cols[j][i] for j in range(size)] for i in range(size)]


def positive_part(n: int, r: float, v: CubeFn) -> CubeFn:
    """P_+ v = (v + r^-1 A_n v) / 2, the projection onto the +r eigenspace."""
    av = signed_adj(n, v)
    return [(v[i] + av[i] / r) / 2 for i in range(len(v))]


def negative_part(n: int, r: float, v: CubeFn) -> CubeFn:
    """P_- v = (v - r^-1 A_n v) / 2, the projection onto the -r eigenspace."""
    av = signed_adj(n, v)
    return [(v[i] - av[i] / r) / 2 for i in range(len(v))]


def max_abs_diff(a: Sequence[float], b: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    return max((abs(x - y) for x, y in zip(a, b)), default=0.0)


def matrix_rank(rows: List[List[float]], tol: float = 1e-9) -> int:
    """Rank by Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting."""
    mat = [row[:] for row in rows]
    nrows, ncols = len(mat), len(mat[0]) if mat else 0
    rank, pivot_row = 0, 0
    for col in range(ncols):
        piv = max(range(pivot_row, nrows), key=lambda i: abs(mat[i][col]), default=None)
        if piv is None or abs(mat[piv][col]) < tol:
            continue
        mat[pivot_row], mat[piv] = mat[piv], mat[pivot_row]
        pv = mat[pivot_row][col]
        for i in range(nrows):
            if i != pivot_row and abs(mat[i][col]) > tol:
                f = mat[i][col] / pv
                mat[i] = [mat[i][j] - f * mat[pivot_row][j] for j in range(ncols)]
        rank += 1
        pivot_row += 1
        if pivot_row == nrows:
            break
    return rank


def demo_signed_cube(seed: int = 271828) -> None:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    print()
    print("=" * 74)
    print("PART II  The signed cube operator  A_{n+1} = [[A_n, I], [I, -A_n]]")
    print("=" * 74)

    print("\nA_2 and A_3 as matrices (rows indexed by vertex bitmask):")
    for n in (2, 3):

For cube dimensions n = 1..8 it evaluates the signed adjacency operator by its O(n 2^n) butterfly recursion and reports machine-precision residuals for additivity, real homogeneity, the square law A_n(A_n v) = n v, the reconstruction identity P_+ v + P_- v = v, the eigenfunction identities A_n P_± v = ±sqrt(n) P_± v, idempotence of each projection, and the vanishing of the mixed composite. demos.code:
"""
Demo B -- The signed Boolean cube: square law, explicit spectral projections,
and the local-density bound for majorities of the cube.

Self-contained (standard library only). Demonstrates, numerically:
  * the recursion A_0 = 0, A_{n+1} = [[A_n, I], [I, -A_n]] evaluated as an
    O(n 2^n) butterfly;
  * additivity and real homogeneity of the operator;
  * the square law A_n(A_n v) = n v;
  * the projections P_+ v = (v + n^-1/2 A_n v)/2 and P_- v = (v - n^-1/2 A_n v)/2,
    which reconstruct v, are eigenfunctions for +-sqrt(n), are idempotent,
    annihilate each other, and have equal ranks 2^(n-1);
  * the consequence: any subset of more than half the cube's vertices contains
    a vertex with at least sqrt(n) neighbours inside the subset.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import random
from typing import Iterable, List, Sequence

CubeFn = List[float]


def signed_adj(n: int, v: CubeFn) -> CubeFn:
    """A_n v, with the leading bit as the high bit of the vertex bitmask."""
    if n == 0:
        return [0.0]
    h = 1 << (n - 1)
    low, high = v[:h], v[h:]
    a_low, a_high = signed_adj(n - 1, low), signed_adj(n - 1, high)
    return [a_low[i] + high[i] for i in range(h)] + [low[i] - a_high[i] for i in range(h)]


def p_plus(n: int, v: CubeFn) -> CubeFn:
    a, r = signed_adj(n, v), math.sqrt(n)
    return [(v[i] + a[i] / r) / 2 for i in range(len(v))]


def p_minus(n: int, v: CubeFn) -> CubeFn:
    a, r = signed_adj(n, v), math.sqrt(n)
    return [(v[i] - a[i] / r) / 2 for i in range(len(v))]


def gap(a: Sequence[float], b: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    return max((abs(x - y) for x, y in zip(a, b)), default=0.0)


def rank(rows: List[List[float]], tol: float = 1e-9) -> int:
    m = [r[:] for r in rows]
    nr, nc = len(m), len(m[0])
    rk = pr = 0
    for c in range(nc):
        if pr >= nr:
            break
        p = max(range(pr, nr), key=lambda i: abs(m[i][c]))
        if abs(m[p][c]) < tol:
            continue
        m[pr], m[p] = m[p], m[pr]
        for i in range(nr):
            if i != pr and abs(m[i][c]) > tol:
                f = m[i][c] / m[pr][c]
                m[i] = [m[i][j] - f * m[pr][j] for j in range(nc)]
        rk += 1
        pr += 1
    return rk


def projection_matrix(n: int, positive: bool) -> List[List[float]]:
    size = 1 << n
    cols = []
    for j in range(size):
        e = [0.0] * size
        e[j] = 1.0
        cols.append(p_plus(n, e) if positive else p_minus(n, e))
    return [[cols[j][i] for j in range(size)] for i in range(size)]


def induced_max_degree(n: int, subset: Iterable[int]) -> int:
    s = set(subset)
    return max(sum(1 for b in range(n) if (x ^ (1 << b)) in s) for x in s)


def main() -> None:
    rng = random.Random(271828)
    print(f"{'n':>3} {'add':>10} {'homog':>10} {'A^2=nI':>10} {'P++P-=id':>10} "
          f"{'A P+=+rP+':>11} {'A P-=-rP-':>11} {'idem':>9} {'orth':>9} {'ranks':>13}")
    for n in range(1, 9):
        size, r = 1 << n, math.sqrt(n)
        v = [rng.uniform(-1, 1) for _ in range(size)]
        w = [rng.uniform(-1, 1) for _ in range(size)]
        c = rng.uniform(-3, 3)
        add = gap(signed_adj(n, [v[i] + w[i] for i in range(size)]),
                  [p + q for p, q in zip(signed_adj(n, v), signed_adj(n, w))])
        hom = gap(signed_adj(n, [c * t for t in v]), [c * t for t in signed_adj(n, v)])
        sq = gap(signed_adj(n, signed_adj(n, v)), [n * t for t in v])
        pp, pm = p_plus(n, v), p_minus(n, v)
        rec = gap([a + b for a, b in zip(pp, pm)], v)
        ep = gap(signed_adj(n, pp), [r * t for t in pp])
        em = gap(signed_adj(n, pm), [-r * t for t in pm])
        idem = gap(p_plus(n, pp), pp)
        orth = max(abs(t) for t in p_minus(n, pp))
        rp, rm = rank(projection_matrix(n, True)), rank(projection_matrix(n, False))
        print(f"{n:>3} {add:>10.1e} {hom:>10.1e} {sq:>10.1e} {rec:>10.1e} "
              f"{ep:>11.1e} {em:>11.1e} {idem:>9.1e} {orth:>9.1e} "
              f"{str(rp) + '+' + str(rm) + '=' + str(size):>13}")
    print("each eigenspace has dimension exactly 2^(n-1): the cube splits in half\n")

    print("Majorities of the cube cannot be locally sparse:")
    print(f"{'n':>3} {'|S|':>7} {'sqrt(n)':>9} {'min max-degree over 300 samples':>34}")
    for n in range(1, 11):
        size = 1 << n
        target = size // 2 + 1
        worst = min(induced_max_degree(n, rng.sample(range(size), target))
                    for _ in range(300))
        print(f"{n:>3} {target:>7} {math.sqrt(n):>9.4f} {worst:>34}")
    print("\nThe bound sqrt(n) is never violated: it is forced by the +sqrt(n)")
    print("eigenspace having dimension exactly half the ambient dimension.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

algorithms.name: First-Disagreement Metric Evaluation, Ball Membership, and Ultrametric Testing
algorithms.description: The computational core of the metric side. Distance evaluation scans coordinates until the first index at which two truth streams disagree and returns 2 raised to minus that index; the scan is lazy, so the cost is O(min(m, D)) oracle calls for a first disagreement at index m under an inspection budget D, independent of how the streams behave afterwards. Ball membership needs no distance at all: because a closed ball of radius 2^-n is precisely the class of streams agreeing below n, membership is decided by n oracle calls with an early exit. Testing the strong triangle inequality on a triple costs three scans, and the sharper isosceles property - the two longest sides of any triangle are equal - is checked by sorting the three distances. The routine distinguishes a proven distance from a budget-limited upper bound, so that an unresolved pair is never silently reported as identical.
algorithms.code:
"""Algorithm 1: first-disagreement metric, ball membership, ultrametric test."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Callable, Optional, Tuple

Stream = Callable[[int], int]  # coordinate oracle: k |-> truth value of statement k


def first_disagreement(x: Stream, y: Stream, budget: int) -> Optional[int]:
    """Least k < budget with x(k) != y(k); None if none is found."""
    for k in range(budget):
        if x(k) != y(k):
            return k
    return None


def cantor_distance(x: Stream, y: Stream, budget: int = 64) -> Tuple[float, bool]:
    """Returns (distance, exact).

    `exact` is False when the two streams agreed throughout the budget, in which
    case the returned value is the upper bound 2^-budget rather than a proven 0.
    """
    m = first_disagreement(x, y, budget)
    if m is None:
        return 2.0 ** (-budget), False
    return 2.0 ** (-m), True


def in_closed_ball(centre: Stream, y: Stream, n: int) -> bool:
    """Decides y in B(centre, 2^-n).

    Correct because a closed ball of radius 2^-n IS the class of streams
    agreeing with the centre on all coordinates below n; only n oracle calls
    per stream are needed, and no distance ever has to be computed.
    """
    return first_disagreement(centre, y, n) is None


def ultrametric_holds(x: Stream, y: Stream, z: Stream, budget: int = 64) -> bool:
    """Checks d(x,z) <= max(d(x,y), d(y,z)) within the inspection budget."""
    dxy, _ = cantor_distance(x, y, budget)
    dyz, _ = cantor_distance(y, z, budget)
    dxz, _ = cantor_distance(x, z, budget)
    return dxz <= max(dxy, dyz) + 1e-15


def isosceles_witness(x: Stream, y: Stream, z: Stream, budget: int = 64) -> bool:
    """Checks the sharper ultrametric fact: the two longest sides are equal."""
    ds = sorted(cantor_distance(a, b, budget)[0] for a, b in ((x, y), (y, z), (x, z)))
    return abs(ds[2] - ds[1]) < 1e-15

algorithms.name: Prefix-Language Enumeration and Transfer-Matrix Box-Dimension Estimation
algorithms.description: Turns dimension into counting. Because closed balls of radius 2^-n are exactly the length-n cylinders, the covering number of a theory at scale 2^-n equals its number N(n) of admissible length-n prefixes exactly, and the box dimension is the limit of log2 N(n)/n - the entropy rate of the prefix language. The generic estimator grows the prefix-closed language breadth-first, extending each admissible word by both bits and filtering; its cost is proportional to the size of the tree actually explored, that is O(sum over k <= n of N(k)) predicate calls, rather than to the ambient 2^n. When the theory is finite-state, enumeration is replaced by linear algebra: the count is a row sum of the n-th power of the transfer matrix, computable in O(n s^2) or O(s^3 log n) operations for s states, and the limiting dimension is simply log2 of the Perron root, obtained by normalised power iteration with geometric convergence governed by the spectral gap.

"""Algorithm 2: prefix-language enumeration, box-dimension estimation, and the
transfer-matrix shortcut for finite-state theories."""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import Callable, List, Sequence, Tuple

Word = Tuple[int, ...]
Predicate = Callable[[Word], bool]


def prefix_levels(admissible: Predicate, nmax: int) -> List[List[Word]]:
    """Levels L_0, ..., L_nmax of the prefix-closed admissible language.

    Grows breadth-first: L_{n+1} = {w + (b,) : w in L_n, b in {0,1}, admissible}.
    Cost: O(sum_k N(k)) predicate calls, i.e. proportional to the size of the
    tree actually explored rather than to 2^nmax.
    """
    levels: List[List[Word]] = [[()]]
    for _ in range(nmax):
        nxt = [w + (b,) for w in levels[-1] for b in (0, 1) if admissible(w + (b,))]
        levels.append(nxt)
    return levels


def box_dimension_estimates(admissible: Predicate, nmax: int) -> List[Tuple[int, int, float]]:
    """(n, N(n), log2 N(n)/n) for n = 1..nmax.

    Justification: closed balls of radius 2^-n are exactly the length-n
    cylinders, so the covering number at scale 2^-n equals N(n) exactly, and
    log(1/2^-n) = n log 2. Hence the box dimension is lim log2 N(n)/n.
    """
    out: List[Tuple[int, int, float]] = []
    for n, level in enumerate(prefix_levels(admissible, nmax)):
        if n >= 1:
            out.append((n, len(level), math.log2(len(level)) / n))
    return out


def walk_counts(matrix: Sequence[Sequence[int]], start: Sequence[int], n: int) -> int:
    """Number of length-n walks: e_start^T M^n 1, by n vector-matrix products.

    For a finite-state theory this replaces enumeration: cost O(n s^2) for s
    states, or O(s^3 log n) with repeated squaring.
    """
    vec = list(start)
    s = len(matrix)
    for _ in range(n):
        vec = [sum(vec[i] * matrix[i][j] for i in range(s)) for j in range(s)]
    return sum(vec)


def power_method_spectral_radius(matrix: Sequence[Sequence[float]],
                                 iters: int = 500) -> float:
    """Perron root of a nonnegative matrix by normalised power iteration.

    For a primitive transfer matrix M the dimension of the theory it presents is
    exactly log2(rho(M)); convergence is geometric in the spectral gap.
    """
    s = len(matrix)
    v = [1.0] * s
    lam = 0.0
    for _ in range(iters):
        w = [sum(matrix[i][j] * v[j] for j in range(s)) for i in range(s)]
        lam = max(abs(t) for t in w)
        if lam == 0.0:
            return 0.0
        v = [t / lam for t in w]
    return lam


def finite_state_dimension(matrix: Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> float:
    """Box dimension of a theory presented by a primitive transfer matrix."""
    return math.log2(power_method_spectral_radius(matrix))

algorithms.name: Butterfly Evaluation of the Signed Cube Operator and Explicit Spectral Splitting
algorithms.description: The computational core of the spectral side. A cube function is stored as an array of 2^n reals indexed by vertex bitmask, with the leading cube coordinate as the high bit, so that the first half of the array is one facet and the second half the other. The operator defined by A_0 = 0 and A_{n+1} = [[A_n, I], [I, -A_n]] is then evaluated by splitting the array, recursing on each half, and recombining with a plus on one facet and a minus on the other: T(2^n) = 2 T(2^(n-1)) + O(2^n) = O(n 2^n), the same butterfly shape as a fast Walsh-Hadamard transform and exponentially cheaper than the O(4^n) dense matrix-vector product. One such evaluation supplies the entire spectral decomposition, since P_± v = (v ± n^(-1/2) A_n v)/2 costs only O(2^n) further arithmetic. The verification routine returns residuals for the square law, the reconstruction identity, both eigenfunction identities, idempotence and orthogonality; the eigenbasis generator projects every vertex indicator, producing a spanning set of the chosen eigenspace of exact dimension 2^(n-1), which makes the decomposition constructive rather than merely existential.
algorithms.pseudocode:
function SIGNED_ADJ(n, v):                 # v has 2^n entries
    if n = 0: return [0]
    h <- 2^(n-1)
    low <- v[0 .. h-1]; high <- v[h .. 2h-1]
    a_low  <- SIGNED_ADJ(n-1, low)
    a_high <- SIGNED_ADJ(n-1, high)
    for i = 0 .. h-1:
        out[i]     <- a_low[i] + high[i]
        out[h + i] <- low[i]  - a_high[i]
    return out                              # cost O(n 2^n)

function SPECTRAL_SPLIT(n, v):              # requires n >= 1
    a <- SIGNED_ADJ(n, v); r <- sqrt(n)
    plus  <- (v + a / r) / 2
    minus <- (v - a / r) / 2
    return (plus, minus)
    # guarantees: plus + minus = v
    #             A_n plus  = +r * plus
    #             A_n minus = -r * minus
    #             P_+ P_+ = P_+,  P_- P_+ = 0

function EIGENBASIS_GENERATOR(n, positive):
    for j = 0 .. 2^n - 1:
        e <- indicator of vertex j
        emit SPECTRAL_SPLIT(n, e)[positive ? 0 : 1]
    # the emitted family spans a space of dimension exactly 2^(n-1)

"""Algorithm 3: butterfly evaluation of the signed cube operator and the
explicit spectral splitting of an arbitrary cube function."""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import List, Sequence, Tuple

CubeFn = List[float]


def signed_adj(n: int, v: Sequence[float]) -> CubeFn:
    """A_n v for the recursion A_0 = 0, A_{n+1} = [[A_n, I], [I, -A_n]].

    The array is indexed by vertex bitmask, the leading cube coordinate being the
    high bit: the first half is the facet 0*, the second half the facet 1*.
    Divide and conquer: T(2^n) = 2 T(2^(n-1)) + O(2^n) = O(n 2^n), the same
    butterfly shape as a fast Walsh-Hadamard transform, versus O(4^n) for a dense
    matrix-vector product.
    """
    if n == 0:
        return [0.0]
    h = 1 << (n - 1)
    low, high = list(v[:h]), list(v[h:])
    a_low, a_high = signed_adj(n - 1, low), signed_adj(n - 1, high)
    return [a_low[i] + high[i] for i in range(h)] + [low[i] - a_high[i] for i in range(h)]


def spectral_split(n: int, v: Sequence[float]) -> Tuple[CubeFn, CubeFn]:
    """Returns (P_+ v, P_- v) with P_± v = (v ± n^(-1/2) A_n v)/2.

    Guarantees, for n >= 1: P_+ v + P_- v = v exactly; A_n(P_± v) = ±sqrt(n) P_± v;
    P_± are idempotent and annihilate each other. Cost: one O(n 2^n) butterfly
    plus O(2^n) arithmetic.
    """
    if n < 1:
        raise ValueError("the splitting requires n >= 1 (A_0 = 0 has no nonzero eigenvalue)")
    a = signed_adj(n, v)
    r = math.sqrt(n)
    plus = [(v[i] + a[i] / r) / 2 for i in range(len(v))]
    minus = [(v[i] - a[i] / r) / 2 for i in range(len(v))]
    return plus, minus


def verify_splitting(n: int, v: Sequence[float]) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Residuals of the four defining identities; all should be ~1e-16."""
    r = math.sqrt(n)
    plus, minus = spectral_split(n, v)
    def gap(a: Sequence[float], b: Sequence[float]) -> float:
        return max(abs(x - y) for x, y in zip(a, b))
    return {
        "square_law": gap(signed_adj(n, signed_adj(n, v)), [n * t for t in v]),
        "reconstruction": gap([p + m for p, m in zip(plus, minus)], v),
        "positive_eigen": gap(signed_adj(n, plus), [r * t for t in plus]),
        "negative_eigen": gap(signed_adj(n, minus), [-r * t for t in minus]),
        "idempotent": gap(spectral_split(n, plus)[0], plus),
        "orthogonal": max(abs(t) for t in spectral_split(n, plus)[1]),
    }


def eigenbasis_generator(n: int, positive: bool = True) -> List[CubeFn]:
    """A spanning set of the ±sqrt(n) eigenspace: project every vertex indicator.

    The resulting family spans a space of dimension exactly 2^(n-1); discarding
    dependent vectors by Gaussian elimination yields a basis. This is the
    constructive content of the spectral splitting: eigenfunctions are produced,
    not merely shown to exist.
    """
    size = 1 << n
    out: List[CubeFn] = []
    for j in range(size):
        e = [0.0] * size
        e[j] = 1.0
        plus, minus = spectral_split(n, e)
        out.append(plus if positive else minus)
    return out

"""
Visualization 1: The geometry of truth space.

Four panels:
  (a) the binary prefix tree with the admissible words of a theory highlighted,
      showing that closed balls of radius 2^-n are exactly the depth-n nodes;
  (b) the "distance matrix" of 64 streams under the first-disagreement metric,
      whose block structure exhibits the nested-or-disjoint ball hierarchy;
  (c) convergence of the box-dimension estimates log2 N(n)/n for three theories;
  (d) the exponential decay of the fair-coin measure bound N(n) 2^-n.

Requires: matplotlib, numpy.  Run:  python3 viz_truth_geometry.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import Callable, List, Tuple

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

Word = Tuple[int, ...]


def paired(w: Word) -> bool:
    return all(w[i] == w[i - 1] for i in range(1, len(w), 2))


def golden(w: Word) -> bool:
    return all(not (w[i] == 1 and w[i + 1] == 1) for i in range(len(w) - 1))


def free(w: Word) -> bool:
    return True


def words(n: int) -> List[Word]:
    out: List[Word] = [()]
    for _ in range(n):
        out = [w + (b,) for w in out for b in (0, 1)]
    return out


def count(pred: Callable[[Word], bool], n: int) -> int:
    return sum(1 for w in words(n) if pred(w))


def first_disagreement_matrix(streams: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    m, depth = streams.shape
    d = np.zeros((m, m))
    for i in range(m):
        for j in range(m):
            diff = np.nonzero(streams[i] != streams[j])[0]
            d[i, j] = 0.0 if diff.size == 0 else 2.0 ** (-int(diff[0]))
    return d


def main() -> None:
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(13.5, 9.5))
    fig.suptitle("The geometry of truth space: prefix balls, ultrametric blocks, dimension",
                 fontsize=14, weight="bold")

    # (a) prefix tree
    ax = axes[0, 0]
    depth = 6
    for d in range(depth + 1):
        ws = words(d)
        for i, w in enumerate(ws):
            x = (i + 0.5) / len(ws)
            y = -d
            if d > 0:
                parent = ws[i][:-1]
                px = (words(d - 1).index(parent) + 0.5) / (len(ws) // 2)
                ok = paired(w)
                ax.plot([px, x], [-(d - 1), y],
                        color="#1f9e86" if ok else "#cccccc",
                        lw=1.2 if ok else 0.5, zorder=1)
            ax.scatter([x], [y], s=9 if paired(w) else 4,
                       color="#1f9e86" if paired(w) else "#cccccc", zorder=2)
    ax.set_title("(a) prefix tree: depth-$n$ nodes = closed balls of radius $2^{-n}$\n"
                 "green = admissible for the paired-dependency theory", fontsize=10)
    ax.set_yticks([-d for d in range(depth + 1)])
    ax.set_yticklabels([f"n={d}" for d in range(depth + 1)], fontsize=8)
    ax.set_xticks([])
    for s in ("top", "right", "bottom"):
        ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)

    # (b) distance matrix
    ax = axes[0, 1]
    rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
    order = np.array(words(6))  # lexicographic prefixes -> block structure
    streams = np.concatenate([order, rng.integers(0, 2, size=(64, 8))], axis=1)
    d = first_disagreement_matrix(streams)
    im = ax.imshow(np.log2(d + 1e-12), cmap="magma")
    ax.set_title("(b) $\\log_2 d(x,y)$ for 64 streams in lexicographic order:\n"
                 "nested blocks — balls are nested or disjoint, never overlapping", fontsize=10)
    fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, fraction=0.046, label="$\\log_2 d$")

    # (c) dimension convergence
    ax = axes[1, 0]
    NMAX = 20
    families = [("anarchy (dim 1)", free, 1.0, "#444444"),
                ("paired dependency (dim 1/2)", paired, 0.5, "#1f9e86"),
                ("golden-mean taboo", golden, math.log2((1 + 5 ** 0.5) / 2), "#d1495b")]
    for name, pred, target, col in families:
        ns = list(range(1, NMAX + 1))
        est = [math.log2(count(pred, n)) / n for n in ns]
        ax.plot(ns, est, "o-", ms=3.5, color=col, label=name)
        ax.axhline(target, ls="--", lw=1, color=col, alpha=0.6)
    ax.set_xlabel("resolution depth $n$")
    ax.set_ylabel("$\\log_2 N(n)/n$")
    ax.set_ylim(0, 1.05)
    ax.set_title("(c) box dimension as the entropy rate of the prefix language", fontsize=10)
    ax.legend(fontsize=8)
    ax.grid(alpha=0.25)

    # (d) measure decay
    ax = axes[1, 1]
    ns = np.arange(1, 61)
    paired_bound = np.array([2.0 ** (math.ceil(n / 2) - n) for n in ns])
    phi = (1 + 5 ** 0.5) / 2
    golden_bound = np.array([(phi / 2.0) ** n for n in ns])
    ax.semilogy(ns, paired_bound, color="#1f9e86", label="paired dependency: $2^{\\lceil n/2\\rceil-n}$")
    ax.semilogy(ns, golden_bound, color="#d1495b", label="golden-mean: $(\\varphi/2)^n$")
    ax.set_xlabel("resolution depth $n$")
    ax.set_ylabel("fair-coin measure bound $N(n)\\,2^{-n}$")
    ax.set_title("(d) dimension $<1$ forces measure zero:\nrandom truth assignments are almost never admissible",
                 fontsize=10)
    ax.legend(fontsize=8)
    ax.grid(alpha=0.25, which="both")

    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 1, 0.95))
    fig.savefig("truth_geometry.png", dpi=160)
    print("wrote truth_geometry.png")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

visualizations.description: A four-panel figure. (b) The eigenvalue histogram of the signed operator superimposed on that of the ordinary hypercube, showing the collapse from n+1 distinct eigenvalues to exactly two, at plus and minus the square root of n, each with multiplicity 2^(n-1). (c) An explicit splitting of a random cube function into its two spectral parts, with reconstruction and eigenvalue residuals printed in the title. """
Visualization 2: The signed cube operator and its two-point spectrum.

Four panels:
  (a) the signed adjacency matrix A_n as a +1/-1/0 image for n = 5;
  (b) the eigenvalue histogram of A_n against that of the unsigned cube,
      showing the collapse from n+1 eigenvalues to just two, at +-sqrt(n),
      each with multiplicity 2^(n-1);
  (c) an explicit splitting v = P_+ v + P_- v of a random cube function;
  (d) the guaranteed local-density bound sqrt(n) against the smallest
      maximum degree observed over random majorities of the cube.

Requires: matplotlib, numpy.  Run:  python3 viz_signed_cube.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import List

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np


def signed_adj_matrix(n: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """A_0 = 0 and A_{n+1} = [[A_n, I], [I, -A_n]]."""
    a = np.zeros((1, 1))
    for k in range(n):
        size = 1 << k
        eye = np.eye(size)
        a = np.block([[a, eye], [eye, -a]])
    return a


def cube_adj_matrix(n: int) -> np.ndarray:
    size = 1 << n
    a = np.zeros((size, size))
    for x in range(size):
        for b in range(n):
            a[x, x ^ (1 << b)] = 1.0
    return a


def min_max_degree(n: int, trials: int, rng: np.random.Generator) -> int:
    size = 1 << n
    target = size // 2 + 1
    worst = n
    for _ in range(trials):
        s = set(rng.choice(size, size=target, replace=False).tolist())
        best = max(sum(1 for b in range(n) if (x ^ (1 << b)) in s) for x in s)
        worst = min(worst, best)
    return worst


def main() -> None:
    rng = np.random.default_rng(2026)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(13.5, 9.5))
    fig.suptitle("The signed Boolean cube: $A_n^2 = nI$, a two-point spectrum, and explicit projections",
                 fontsize=14, weight="bold")

    n = 5
    a = signed_adj_matrix(n)

    # (a) the matrix
    ax = axes[0, 0]
    im = ax.imshow(a, cmap="coolwarm", vmin=-1, vmax=1)
    ax.set_title(f"(a) the signed adjacency matrix $A_{{{n}}}$ (red $+1$, blue $-1$)", fontsize=10)
    fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, fraction=0.046)
    resid = float(np.max(np.abs(a @ a - n * np.eye(1 << n))))
    ax.set_xlabel(f"$\\max|A^2 - nI| = {resid:.1e}$")

    # (b) spectra
    ax = axes[0, 1]
    ev_signed = np.linalg.eigvalsh(a)
    ev_plain = np.linalg.eigvalsh(cube_adj_matrix(n))
    ax.hist(ev_plain, bins=np.arange(-n - 1.5, n + 2.5, 1.0), alpha=0.55,
            color="#888888", label="unsigned cube: $n+1$ eigenvalues")
    ax.hist(ev_signed, bins=60, alpha=0.85, color="#1f9e86",
            label="signed cube: only $\\pm\\sqrt{n}$")
    ax.axvline(math.sqrt(n), ls="--", color="#d1495b")
    ax.axvline(-math.sqrt(n), ls="--", color="#d1495b")
    ax.set_title(f"(b) spectrum collapse at $n={n}$: two eigenvalues,\n"
                 f"each of multiplicity $2^{{n-1}} = {1 << (n - 1)}$", fontsize=10)
    ax.set_xlabel("eigenvalue")
    ax.legend(fontsize=8)

    # (c) the splitting
    ax = axes[1, 0]
    v = rng.uniform(-1, 1, size=1 << n)
    r = math.sqrt(n)
    av = a @ v
    pp, pm = (v + av / r) / 2, (v - av / r) / 2
    idx = np.arange(1 << n)
    ax.bar(idx - 0.28, v, width=0.28, color="#888888", label="$v$")
    ax.bar(idx, pp, width=0.28, color="#1f9e86", label="$P_+v$ (eigenvalue $+\\sqrt{n}$)")
    ax.bar(idx + 0.28, pm, width=0.28, color="#d1495b", label="$P_-v$ (eigenvalue $-\\sqrt{n}$)")
    err_r = float(np.max(np.abs(pp + pm - v)))
    err_p = float(np.max(np.abs(a @ pp - r * pp)))
    ax.set_title("(c) $v = P_+v + P_-v$ with $P_\\pm v=\\frac{1}{2}(v\\pm n^{-1/2}A_nv)$\n"
                 f"reconstruction error {err_r:.1e}, eigen-error {err_p:.1e}", fontsize=10)
    ax.set_xlabel("cube vertex (bitmask)")
    ax.legend(fontsize=8)

    # (d) degree bound
    ax = axes[1, 1]
    ns = list(range(1, 11))
    obs = [min_max_degree(k, 200, rng) for k in ns]
    ax.bar(ns, obs, color="#1f9e86", alpha=0.85,
           label="smallest max-degree over 200 random majorities")
    ax.plot(ns, [math.sqrt(k) for k in ns], "o--", color="#d1495b",
            label="guaranteed bound $\\sqrt{n}$")
    ax.set_xlabel("cube dimension $n$")
    ax.set_ylabel("maximum induced degree")
    ax.set_title("(d) every set of more than half the vertices contains\n"
                 "a vertex with $\\geq\\sqrt{n}$ neighbours inside it", fontsize=10)
    ax.legend(fontsize=8)
    ax.grid(alpha=0.25)

    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 1, 0.95))
    fig.savefig("signed_cube_spectrum.png", dpi=160)
    print("wrote signed_cube_spectrum.png")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

The first panel draws the binary prefix tree, highlights the closed balls at a chosen resolution depth, and greys out the words forbidden by a selectable constraint rule (total anarchy, paired dependency, the golden-mean consistency taboo, or period-three rules with one or two free coordinates), reporting the admissible count N(n) alongside the estimate log2 N(n)/n and the exact dimension. The second panel shows three truth streams whose individual bits can be clicked and flipped, recomputing all three pairwise distances live and testing both the strong triangle inequality and the sharper isosceles property, with a scaled drawing of the resulting triangle. The third panel plots log2 N(n)/n out to depth forty against the exact dimension, tabulates the values, and displays the fair-coin measure bound - letting a reader watch sparsity and abundance emerge simultaneously from the same counting sequence.

interactive_demos.title: The Signed Cube Laboratory: Splitting Every Function into Plus and Minus Root-n Halves
interactive_demos.description: An interactive workbench for the spectral half of the theory. Choose the cube dimension from one to seven and a test function (random values, a single vertex spike, the parity checkerboard, a first-coordinate sign pattern, or an index ramp); the widget evaluates the signed operator by its butterfly recursion and draws the function alongside its two spectral parts as interleaved bars, so the reader sees the reconstruction identity directly. A live verification panel reports machine-precision residuals for the square law, reconstruction, both eigenfunction identities, idempotence and orthogonality, together with the ranks of the two projections, which always come out as 2^(n-1) each. A second view renders the signed adjacency matrix as a coloured grid, and a final panel samples random majorities of the cube, plotting the smallest induced maximum degree found against the guaranteed square-root-of-n bound, with the full interlacing argument hidden behind an expandable panel.
interactive_demos.html:
The Signed Cube Laboratory

Put a real number on every vertex of the n-dimensional cube. The ordinary cube operator replaces each value by the sum of its n neighbours. Flip some signs — following the recursion An+1 = [[An, I], [I, −An]] — and something extraordinary happens: An2 = n·Id. The operator becomes a square root of n, its spectrum collapses to just ±√n, and every function splits explicitly into a +√n half and a −√n half by P±v = ½(v ± n−1/2Anv). Play with it below.

The operator and the splitting

Grey = v. Green = P₊v. Pink = P₋v. They always add back to v, and each half is an exact eigenfunction.

The signed matrix An

Green cell = +1, pink = −1, dark = 0. Every row has exactly n nonzero entries: the signed cube is the hypercube graph with half its edges negated.

Why the halving matters: majorities of the cube cannot be sparse

Because the two eigenspaces have exactly equal dimension 2n−1, any set S of more than half the vertices must support a nonzero +√n eigenfunction — and that forces some vertex of S to have at least √n neighbours inside S. Sample random majorities below and watch the bound hold, every time.

Click to reveal the argument in full

The space of real functions on the cube has dimension 2n. The functions supported on S form a subspace of dimension |S| ≥ 2n−1+1; the +√n eigenspace has dimension exactly 2n−1 (the trace of the signed operator is zero, so the two eigenvalues have equal multiplicity). Two subspaces whose dimensions sum to more than the ambient dimension intersect nontrivially, so there is a nonzero eigenfunction living entirely on S. Restricting the operator to S and applying Cauchy's interlacing theorem, the largest eigenvalue of that restriction is at least √n. But the largest eigenvalue of any signed adjacency matrix is bounded by the maximum degree of the underlying graph. Hence some vertex of S has ≥ √n neighbours in S. Translating this statement about cube subsets into a statement about Boolean functions is exactly what resolves the long-standing question of whether the sensitivity of a Boolean function is polynomially related to its degree.

# Close Proofs: The Fractal Dimension of Mathematical Truth *A guided tour of two ways to measure a Boolean cube — by counting, and by spectra.* --- ## 0. The question How long is the coast of Britain? The honest answer is a counter-question: *at what scale?* Measure with a hundred-kilometre ruler and you get one number; with a metre stick, a far larger one. The coastline has no length, but it does have a **dimension** — a number between $1$ and $2$ measuring how fast detail proliferates as you zoom in. More than a curve, less than a region. This page asks the same question about **truth**. Line up every statement of a formal language in a fixed order, $\varphi_0, \varphi_1, \varphi_2, \dots$, and record which are true and which are false as an infinite string of bits. A complete worldview becomes a single point in the space of infinite binary streams; a theory becomes a *subset* of that space. Subsets have dimensions. And for the model we will build, the dimension is exactly $\tfrac12$ — sparse enough to be vanishingly rare among all conceivable assignments, rich enough to be uncountably abundant. By the end of this page you will have: - built a metric on worldviews and discovered that it obeys a *stronger* triangle inequality than Euclidean space; - watched box-counting dimension turn into pure combinatorics — counting admissible prefixes; - computed the dimension of several theories yourself, and seen it equal an eigenvalue; - met a second ruler for Boolean cubes: an operator that squares to $n$ times the identity and splits every function on the cube into two explicit halves — the algebraic core of a famous complexity theorem. --- ## 1. A ruler for worldviews Two accounts of the mathematical universe are indistinguishable until they disagree about something. The deeper into the list that first disagreement lies, the harder they are to tell apart. So define the **first-disagreement distance** between two truth streams $x$ and $y$: $$d(x,y) = \begin{cases} 0, & x = y,\\ 2^{-m}, & m = \min\{k : x_k \neq y_k\}.\end{cases}$$ Two theories that agree about the first thousand statements sit within $2^{-1000}$; two that disagree about $\varphi_0$ sit at the maximum distance $1$. *Close proofs are proofs that disagree late.* Two facts make this ruler extraordinary, and both are visible in the widget below. > **Theorem (Balls are prefix classes).** For all truth streams $x,y$ and every $n$, > $$d(x,y) \le 2^{-n} \iff x_k = y_k \text{ for all } k < n.$$ > The closed ball of radius $2^{-n}$ is exactly the set of streams sharing the first $n$ truth values. > **Theorem (Truth is ultrametric).** For all $x,y,z$, > $$d(x,z) \le \max\bigl(d(x,y), d(y,z)\bigr).$$ The second is the *strong* triangle inequality, and it is a genuine strengthening: it says the longest side of any triangle can never exceed the longer of the other two. Spaces satisfying it are called [ultrametric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultrametric_space), and they behave in ways a Euclidean eye finds alien. Every triangle is isosceles. Every point of a ball is a centre of it. Any two balls are nested or disjoint — they never partially overlap.
Click to reveal the proofs (both are three lines) *Balls are prefix classes.* If $x$ and $y$ agree below $n$, then either $x = y$ (distance $0$) or their first disagreement occurs at some index $m \ge n$, so $d = 2^{-m} \le 2^{-n}$. Conversely, if they already disagree at some $k < n$, the first disagreement index satisfies $m \le k < n$, so $d = 2^{-m} \ge 2^{-(n-1)} > 2^{-n}$. *Ultrametricity.* Let $\mu = \max(d(x,y), d(y,z))$. If $\mu = 0$ then $x = y = z$ and there is nothing to prove; otherwise $\mu = 2^{-n}$ for some $n$, since the distance function only takes the values $0$ and $2^{-n}$. By the first theorem, $x$ agrees with $y$ below $n$ and $y$ agrees with $z$ below $n$; agreement to a fixed depth is *transitive*, so $x$ agrees with $z$ below $n$, and the first theorem read backwards gives $d(x,z) \le 2^{-n} = \mu$. Notice what happened: the strong triangle inequality is *nothing but* the transitivity of prefix agreement, transported across the equivalence between balls and cylinders. No analysis is involved at all.
Play with the tree, flip bits by clicking them, and try — you will fail — to build a triangle that violates the strong inequality. {{interactive_demo:0}} --- ## 2. Dimension = counting = entropy rate In Euclidean space, [box-counting dimension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minkowski%E2%80%93Bouligand_dimension) covers a set with boxes of side $\varepsilon$, counts how many are needed — call it $N(\varepsilon)$ — and takes $$\dim_B = \lim_{\varepsilon\to0}\frac{\log N(\varepsilon)}{\log(1/\varepsilon)} .$$ A segment needs $N \approx 1/\varepsilon$ boxes and gets dimension $1$; a filled square needs $N\approx\varepsilon^{-2}$ and gets $2$; the classical middle-thirds Cantor set gets $\log 2/\log 3 \approx 0.6309$. Here the first theorem does something delightful. Balls of radius $2^{-n}$ **are** the length-$n$ prefix classes, so $N(2^{-n})$ is simply the number of length-$n$ prefixes a theory permits. Geometry evaporates and combinatorics remains: $$\boxed{\ \dim_B = \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log_2 N(n)}{n}\ }$$ The dimension of a theory is its **entropy rate**: the average number of genuinely new bits per statement. Total logical anarchy, with every pattern admissible, gives $N(n) = 2^n$ and dimension $1$. A categorical theory that pins down every truth value gives $N(n) = 1$ and dimension $0$. Real mathematics is in between. ### The model: half discovery, half bookkeeping Suppose statements come in *linked pairs*: $\varphi_{2k}$ is an independent assertion, freely true or false, and $\varphi_{2k+1}$ is logically equivalent to it — a restatement whose truth value carries no new information. Then the admissible prefixes of length $n$ number exactly $N(n) = 2^{\lceil n/2 \rceil}$. > **Theorem (Truth has a nontrivial fractal dimension).** This truth set has box dimension exactly > $$\dim_B = \tfrac12, \qquad\text{so in particular}\qquad 0 < \dim_B < 1 .$$ The computation is a squeeze: $\log_2 N(n)/n = \lceil n/2\rceil/n \in [\tfrac12, \tfrac12 + \tfrac1{2n}]$. The two inequalities carry all the meaning.
Why dimension below 1 means truth is a measure-zero dust Under the fair-coin measure — flip an independent unbiased coin for each statement — each length-$n$ cylinder has probability $2^{-n}$, so the theory has probability at most $N(n)2^{-n} = 2^{\lceil n/2\rceil - n}$, which goes to $0$ exponentially. With probability $1$, a randomly generated worldview eventually affirms a statement and denies its own restatement. **Random truth is almost never truth.** More generally, any theory of upper dimension strictly less than $1$ is null, because $N(n)2^{-n} = 2^{\,n(\log_2 N(n)/n\ -\ 1)} \to 0$.
Why dimension above 0 means truth is uncountably abundant Positive box dimension rules out any countable compact set (those all have dimension $0$). In fact the coordinate-doubling map $(a_0,a_1,a_2,\dots) \mapsto (a_0,a_0,a_1,a_1,a_2,a_2,\dots)$ is a homeomorphism from the whole stream space onto our truth set, so it has cardinality continuum and is a Cantor set in its own right. There are continuum-many complete admissible extensions, and no finite or countable list captures them: [incompleteness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G%C3%B6del%27s_incompleteness_theorems) rendered as geometry — there is always another independent bit further out.
Nothing is special about "evens free, odds forced": if the free coordinates are the residues $R$ modulo $m$, the dimension is $|R|/m$, so every rational value in $[0,1]$ is realised. The widget above lets you switch between several such rules and watch the estimate converge. The same cube, measured a different way Prefixes of length $n$ are the vertices of the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube $Q_n = \{0,1\}^n$. Everything so far was a statement about *how many* vertices survive as $n$ grows. There is a second, entirely different way to measure a subset of a *fixed* cube, and it is sharper. Hang minus signs on the edges. Define an operator on functions $v : Q_n \to \mathbb{R}$ by $A_0 = 0$ and $$A_{n+1} = \begin{pmatrix} A_n & I \\ I & -A_n\end{pmatrix}, \qquad A_1 = \begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}.$$ Delete the minus sign and this is the ordinary cube adjacency operator, whose spectrum spreads over the $n+1$ values $n, n-2, \dots, -n$. The operator is a square root of $n$. Its spectrum has collapsed from $n+1$ values to just two, $\pm\sqrt n$. And the splitting can be written down explicitly rather than merely inferred: > **Theorem (Spectral splitting).** Let $r \neq 0$ with $r^2 = n$, and set > $$P_+ v = \tfrac12\bigl(v + r^{-1}A_nv\bigr), \qquad P_- v = \tfrac12\bigl(v - r^{-1}A_nv\bigr).$$ > Then $P_+v + P_-v = v$, $\;A_n(P_+v) = r\,P_+v$, and $A_n(P_-v) = -r\,P_-v$. The two operators are > complementary projections: $P_\pm^2 = P_\pm$ and $P_+P_- = P_-P_+ = 0$. Since $A_n$ has trace zero, each > eigenspace has dimension exactly $2^{n-1}$.

Why the exact halving matters Here is the payoff. Suppose you select **more than half** the vertices of the cube — any $2^{n-1}+1$ of them — and look at the graph they induce. > **Theorem (Majorities of the cube are locally dense).** Any set of more than half the vertices of $Q_n$ > contains a vertex with at least $\sqrt n$ neighbours inside the set.
Click to reveal the argument The functions supported on your chosen set $S$ form a subspace of dimension $|S| \ge 2^{n-1}+1$. The $+\sqrt n$ eigenspace has dimension exactly $2^{n-1}$. Two subspaces of a $2^n$-dimensional space whose dimensions sum to more than $2^n$ must intersect nontrivially — so there is a nonzero $+\sqrt n$ eigenfunction living entirely on $S$. Restrict the operator to $S$; by [Cauchy interlacing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poincar%C3%A9_separation_theorem), the restriction has largest eigenvalue at least $\sqrt n$. But the largest eigenvalue of any signed adjacency matrix is at most the maximum degree of the underlying graph. Hence some vertex of $S$ has $\ge \sqrt n$ neighbours in $S$. This is [Huang's theorem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sensitivity_theorem) (2019), and via a translation due to Gotsman and Linial it settles the **sensitivity conjecture**: the sensitivity of a Boolean function is polynomially related to its degree, block sensitivity, certificate complexity, and every other standard complexity measure. A thirty-year-old question in theoretical computer science, answered by two well-placed minus signs.
The explicit projections make this *constructive*: to produce the witnessing eigenfunction, apply $P_+$ to any function it does not annihilate. Existence proofs become recipes. --- ## 5. Two rulers, one cube Stand back and the two halves rhyme. | | **metric ruler** | **spectral ruler** | |---|---|---| | measures | subsets of $Q_n$ as $n \to \infty$ | subsets of a fixed $Q_n$ | | invariant | growth rate of $\lvert S_n\rvert$ | eigenvalues of a structured operator | | says | a theory keeping $2^{n/2}$ prefixes has dimension $\tfrac12$: a null but uncountable dust | keep more than half the vertices and you cannot avoid local density $\sqrt n$ | | blind to | how the surviving vertices are arranged | sets much smaller than half the cube | And they touch. For a theory defined by *local* constraints, the count $N(n)$ obeys a linear recurrence and the dimension is $\log_2$ of a spectral radius — the golden-mean taboo giving $\log_2\varphi \approx 0.694$. The fractal dimension of truth is an eigenvalue in disguise; in particular it is always the base-two logarithm of an algebraic number. --- ## 6. Where this goes next Five concrete conjectures the framework suggests: 1. **Periodic-coordinate dimension formula.** For every period $m$ and every set of free residues $R$, the corresponding truth set has *Hausdorff* dimension $|R|/m$, not merely box dimension. 2. **Hausdorff/box agreement.** For every periodic-coordinate theory, the two notions of dimension coincide. 3. **Bi-Lipschitz invariance under bounded reordering.** If a permutation of the enumeration moves each index by at most a fixed constant, it preserves the dimension of every theory — the dimension of truth should not depend on inessential re-cataloguing. 4. **Finite-state truth dimensions are algebraic.** Any theory presented by a finite graph with adjacency matrix $A$ has dimension $\log_2\rho(A)$, hence the base-two logarithm of an algebraic number. 5. **Golden-mean truth set.** The no-two-consecutive-truths theory has Hausdorff *and* box dimension $\log_2\bigl((1+\sqrt5)/2\bigr)$, strictly between $0$ and $1$. What to take away **Truth has a shape.** Declare two worldviews close when they agree deep into a fixed enumeration, and a rigid geometry appears unbidden: balls are prefix classes, the strong triangle inequality holds, and the space is a compact ultrametric Cantor set of hierarchically nested clusters. **That shape has a dimension strictly between $0$ and $1$.** For the model built here it is exactly $\tfrac12$: measure zero under fair coin flips, yet of cardinality continuum. Half discovery, half bookkeeping. **The same cubes yield to spectra.** Signing half the cube's edges produces an operator squaring to $n$ times the identity, with explicit complementary projections onto two eigenspaces of equal dimension $2^{n-1}$ — and that exact halving is what forbids any majority of cube vertices from being locally sparse. Coastlines, theories, and Boolean functions are not obviously the same subject. What unites them is that each is a story about how structure multiplies as you zoom in, and about how — with the right ruler — you can put a number on it.

/-!
# The metric and fractal dimension of truth

This file joins the existing first-disagreement metric on Boolean truth streams
with the existing box-counting theory of accepted finite prefixes.  It does not
introduce a second encoding: `FractalTruthMetric.Cantor` supplies the metric,
and `TruthFractalDimension.truthSet` supplies the prefix family.

this model of truth is sparse (dimension below the ambient value `1`) but not
negligible (positive dimension).

an equivalence class of streams having the same first `n` truth values. -/
theorem closedBall_scale_iff_prefix (x y : ℕ → Bool) (n : ℕ) :
    cantorDist x y ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(n : ℤ)) ↔ AgreeTo n x y := by
  exact cantorDist_le_iff_agreeTo x y n

/-- The first-disagreement distance obeys the strong triangle inequality. -/

    cantorDist x z ≤ max (cantorDist x y) (cantorDist y z) := by
  exact cantorDist_ultra x y z
